newsitem.title: UK: EMI plans special centenary music releases.
newsitem.headline: EMI plans special centenary music releases.

text.p: EMI Group Plc said on Wednesday it was planning a series of commemorative music releases to mark the company's centenary this year.
Artists such as David Bowie, Freddie Mercury, Frank Sinatra, John Lennon and Pink Floyd will be showcased in a limited edition re-issue series of 20 classic albums in their original vinyl format.

A collection of CDs will feature hits from top EMI artists, remastered with the latest technology and issued with extra tracks and special packaging. A 10-CD boxed set will trace the company's classical recording history.

New releases include a studio recording of Paul McCartney's "Standing Stone" symphony and a collection with the working title "EMI sings EMI" comprising the songs of some of EMI's best known artists, recorded by the pick of the current roster.
EMI traces its roots back to The Gramophone Company, founded in 1897.

Chairman Sir Colin Southgate on Wednesday launched a new charity, the Music Sound Foundation, to promote and support music over the next 100 years. Its initial patrons are Sir George Martin, Sir Simon Rattle and Sir Cliff Richard.
EMI plans an exhibition and a series of concerts to mark its centenary and to help raise the initial capital for the charity.
